system: You write the SCRIPT step of QuickFrame, a stickman/whiteboard explainer-video pipeline (topic -> script -> storyboard -> animation -> captions+music -> render -> publish). Your script becomes the storyboard: one short scene per beat, in the spine's beat order. Write for the EAR, not the eye: short spoken sentences a person reads aloud in one breath. Never invent statistics, prices, or facts. If a claim is assumed, keep it generic. The narration (vo) must be specific to THIS topic — do not echo generic template lines. onText is the words TYPESET onto the frame by the encoder, not painted into an image. Keep it <= 6 words. Return ONLY a single JSON object that matches the schema. No prose, no markdown fences.
user:
TOPIC: why airplane mode still drains your battery overnight
SPINE: Inside the system — Open up a process or product and show the hidden machinery and tradeoffs.
TONE: clear, friendly, confident
VOICE RATE: 1x   ASPECT: 16:9   TARGET LENGTH: 30s

Write exactly 5 scenes, one per beat, in this order:
  1. The surface — Show what the user sees and takes for granted. (default shot: hero)
  2. Under the hood — Reveal the first layer of real machinery. (default shot: f2)
  3. The hidden step — Name the step nobody thinks about but everything depends on. (default shot: s5)
  4. The tradeoff — Explain the cost or compromise built into the design. (default shot: s6)
  5. The big picture — Zoom out to why the whole thing is built this way. (default shot: f1)

Size each scene's narration to about 16 words so the whole script lands near 30s.
Use only these frame ids for art: hero, f2, s5, s6, f1 (you may reassign among them, but keep them distinct across scenes).

Return JSON matching this schema:
